note_tweet.text:
OpenAI just dropped Dots — those always-on AI agents that live in ChatGPT, each with its own cloud computer and browser. Cool idea. The problem? It’s locked inside their product.

There’s a solid open-source take on the same concept: OpenDots.

It’s a self-hosted template for persistent AI coworkers. Each “Dot” can have its own computer, browser, tools, and workspace. You run the whole thing locally on your machine (or your own server), so your data stays with you. Setup is straightforward — clone the repo, drop in your own API key (OpenAI or any compatible provider), and you’re running. No forced subscription to ChatGPT Pro just to get agents that keep working when you close the tab.

What I like about it:
- Each agent gets a clear role, instructions, and permissions.
- You stay in the loop with approval steps before it does anything risky.
- You can connect tools and apps, and there’s even a live computer view so you can watch it work (or jump in when needed).
- Conversations and documents live in your own workspace.

It’s still early and evolving, but the direction is clear: the always-on agent idea without handing everything over to one company.

Repo is here if you want to try it:  
https://t.co/nLP0uZuzdD

Anyone else playing with local/self-hosted agent setups lately? Curious what’s actually sticking for people beyond the demo stage.

"oops you misspelled muse." That's Meta's Alexandr Wang, replying to OpenAI's Tibo Sottiaux after he posted a DM-if-interested call to help scale dots to a billion users. Sottiaux came back with "quit posting butts and go buy containers... celebrate your 12 users," a jab at Muse's plush mascot marketing and Meta's data center spend. Wang's answer was an App Store screenshot: Muse number one in Productivity, ChatGPT two, Claude three, Gemini four. Someone from SpaceX then posted a meme of Muse and OpenAI brawling while Grok Bot cooks quietly in the corner. Half a million views before lunch.

Funny, and beside the point. Muse hit 10 million US downloads in its first 40 days after launching September 8, genuinely fast. Then daily downloads dropped to about 165,000 in the week ending October 7, down 8.1 percent week over week, and Hunterbrook Capital disclosed a short against Meta on October 9 citing that exact slowdown. OpenAI's dots and xAI's Grok are tracing the same shaped curve a few weeks behind.

Here's what the trash talk skips over. Amazon has blocked Muse from checking out on its site since September 20. JPMorgan and Schwab won't let any outside agent log into an account or move money. Delta has zero third party booking integration for agents, full stop. Every lab racing to put an always-on agent in a billion pockets is hitting the same wall: the places people actually spend money don't want agents near their checkout yet.

Download charts make a great screenshot. They don't fix the fact that Amazon, two major banks, and a top airline have all said no.

Constraint Lock: Always-on agent access

Task: Trigger a specialized AI agent with a voice command and have it act as a persistent teammate (calendar, research, calls, notes) without opening an app.

What broke before:
Agents lived inside chat windows or required multiple taps and context switching. Voice wake words were locked to the phone’s default assistant.

The lock:
A custom iOS Shortcut that opens Grok Bot voice chat on “Hey Grok.” Each agent gets its own cloud computer. SpaceX is already advertising the model in Penn Station as always-on teammates for 600k+ daily commuters.

Result:
The constraint moves from “can the model respond?” to “can the agent stay useful across real interruptions, handoffs, and ongoing tasks without constant human babysitting?”

Principle:
When agents become always-on, the quality of the initial constraints and role definition matters more than the trigger. A weak lock fails the moment the agent is running unsupervised in the background.

The next wave isn't AI you talk to. It's AI that keeps working after you close the laptop.

Three big players just lined up for it:

🟠 Claude Duet (Anthropic): a morning brief, keeps an eye on your connected apps, and only pings you when it matters.
⚫ Grok Bot (xAI): plugs into your phone apps and helps run your life and business.

Same promise, three very different bets.

Spear Street Technology Instinct: A zero-UI, computer-use personal assistant driven by ambient messaging and cloud desktop OS automation.
Meta Muse: An asynchronous personal agent platform featuring secure virtual compute isolation (Muse Secure VM), dual-agent gatekeepers, and Stripe Link financial encapsulation.
OpenClaw: A local-first personal agent runtime governed by the OpenClaw Foundation, utilizing multi-channel messaging adapters and autonomous background Heartbeat daemons.
Cross-Platform Orchestration: Unified bridging protocols combining Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateways and Agent2Agent (A2A) cryptographic cards.

Key Operational Frameworks & Platform Mechanics1. Google Gemini Spark
Primitives: Operates on four core pillars: Tasks (strategic goals), Schedules (cron/email triggers), Skills (procedural instructions via SKILL.md), and Connected Apps (bi-directional Google Workspace and MCP integrations).
Governance Model: Categorized into Low Tier (read-only analysis), Medium Tier (internal document updates and calendar event drafting), and High Tier (external actions, financial checkouts, and credential entry requiring a manual "Take Over" gate).
Directive Standard: Utilizes the RISEN framework (Role, Input, Steps, Execution constraints, Next-state goal) for robust prompt engineering.
2. xAI Grok Automations & Prompt Systems
Architecture: Distinguishes between stateless Grok Automations (cron/email triggers), persistent Grok Bot (multi-app cloud VMs), and terminal-native Grok Build.
Modes & Capabilities: Features dual behavioral registers (Regular Mode for high density/neutral analysis and Fun Mode for satirical personas), DeepSearch (multi-hop web and social X crawling loops), and Think Mode (deliberative chain-of-thought token allocation).
3. Hermes Agent & Bot Mode
Learning Loop: Implements a closed four-stage loop: observation, distillation, dynamic reuse, and iterative refinement.
Prompt Tiers: Partitions system prompts into a Stable Tier (SOUL.md and core protocol cache), Context Tier (repository rules), and Volatile Tier (ephemeral memory snapshots).
Bot Mode Swarms: Restructures execution into isolated profiles stored at ~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/, maintaining independent memory banks (bank_id), heterogeneous model configurations, and inter-bot CLI dispatches.
4. Instinct (Spear Street Technology)
Zero-UI Experience: Interacts with users exclusively via messaging rails (iMessage, WhatsApp, SMS) and voice telephony.
Execution Engine: Combines structured API workflows with vision-language models (VLMs) for OS automation, DOM navigation, and multi-factor authentication (TOTP/2FA) resolution.
Enterprise Security, Governance, and Risk Management
Indirect Prompt Injection Defenses: Inbound unstructured data (such as emails or scraped web pages) must be explicitly delimited and treated as untrusted text to prevent malicious payload execution.
Least-Privilege Principles: Production deployments require scoping OAuth tokens and provisioning dedicated service accounts with read-only permissions for automated analytical routines.
Context Economics: Systems must manage token burn by segmenting tasks into bounded sessions (/new), applying compaction strategies (/compress), and offloading procedures to progressive-disclosure skill files (SKILL.md).
